articles.summary: BOSTON, Mass., October 8, 2026 Ginkgo Bioworks Holdings, Inc. (we, us, our and the Company) recently discovered an unauthorized third party accessed data (Affected Data) from cloud environments primarily associated with the Companys former biosecurity business. We took immediate steps to secure our systems and investigate the situation. What actions we took We launched an investigation with assistance from an independent third-party cybersecurity response team and forensic experts at a leading national forensic firm, together with outside counsel. The investigation is ongoing. We implemented our cybersecurity response plan consistent with our previously established cyber incident protocols. We informed the FBI of this incident and are cooperating with federal law enforcement in the investigation. We believe we have notified all of our customers whose data was included in the Affected Data

articles.summary: Ginkgo Bioworks (NYSE: DNA) today announced that it will provide in-kind access to its autonomous laboratory in Boston to support the National Science Foundation’s X-Labs program. Ginkgo’s support was announced today by Michael Kratsios, Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit in Washington, D.C. NSF X-Labs is a $1.5 billion, decade-long initiative to fund independent teams of researchers, engineers, and entrepreneurs pursuing breakthrough science through milestone-based awards. Through its contribution, Ginkgo will make cloud lab time on its autonomous lab available to NSF X-Labs teams, giving researchers remote access to robotic lab infrastructure to design, run, and analyze experiments.
